leading_positions.synthesis: Targeted protein degradation is in the preferred configuration of three members. Aili and Chabes propose Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for induced-proximity degraders; Somfai includes B038 only as a second part beside B058 and, because of the three-person cap, would credit Crews alone, so the laureate sets differ. All three acknowledge that the thalidomide-cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) and Sakamoto are not covered by a PROTAC citation, and all three note that no PROTAC is yet approved. They differ on whether the missing approval and the glue strand weigh against a prize now.

Base editing is in the preferred configuration of three members, each as a Liu-only credit (Aqvist moved from Liu, Komor and Gaudelli to Liu alone after discussion). Aqvist proposes it as the whole prize, while Sparr pairs it with B065 and Zou pairs it with B064. All three leave out Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo, and all three treat the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Target-AID priority question as open points. Shared: replication, adoption and early clinical use. Not shared: whether it stands alone or as one part of a two-part prize.

Nitrogenase is in the preferred configuration of two members, but the laureate sets differ: Brzezinski proposes Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt, while Zou proposes only Rees and Einsle and anchors the citation on the cofactor structure. Both agree that the full catalytic mechanism is unresolved and that Dean and Ribbe have real claims. Zou combines it with B011, whereas Brzezinski presents it alone.

Nanopore sensing is the preferred configuration of one member (the chair), proposing Deamer, Bayley and Akeson. Several members (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski, Chabes, Somfai, Zou) say the three-name cut leaves out Branton and Kasianowicz, and Somfai questions whether the achievement is analytical engineering or molecule-making. It appears as an alternative for Aili, Chabes and Zou.

Somfai alone proposes a two-part prize pairing Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) with a Crews-only degrader credit. No other member lists B058 among preferences, and others question whether it adds enough to the 2010 cross-coupling prize.

Sparr alone proposes pairing phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne) with a Liu-only base-editing credit. She acknowledges that Rosen is excluded only by the three-person cap. Aqvist, Somfai and Aili regard phase separation as still contested or too early.

Zou alone proposes a two-part prize pairing a nitrogenase structure (Rees, Einsle) with Liu-only base editing. Zou concedes that no other member ranked nitrogenase first, and Somfai raises the same mechanism-versus-structure reservation.

areas_of_agreement: No configuration reaches the five-member majority: the explicit first-choice counts are B038 with three members, B011 with three, B064 with two, and B003 with one, with B058 and B065 each appearing only in a single member's two-part configuration.

Every member who discussed it accepts that base editing is mature in adoption and that the 2020 CRISPR prize is the main framing risk; Aqvist, Chabes, Sparr and Zou favour Liu alone as the cleanest attribution.
Every member who discussed B038 accepts that the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands are separate discoveries that a three-person citation cannot both honour.
Members agree that a nanopore citation faces a five-way priority problem (Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz, Bayley, Akeson) with three slots.

Members broadly agree that any citation should rest on what is settled (nitrogenase cofactor structure rather than mechanism; phase separation as a demonstrated phenomenon rather than a claim about every condensate).
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing is a distinct chemical advance (programmed nucleobase deamination and directed evolution of deaminases) or an engineering extension of the CRISPR platform recognised in 2020; Somfai, Brzezinski, Linke and Aili press this, Aqvist, Zou and Sparr defend the chemistry.
Whether nanopore sequencing is analytical chemistry, with a new transduction principle, or genomics and instrumentation (Linke versus Somfai and Aili).

Whether phase separation is settled enough as a concept: Sparr separates the demonstrated phenomenon from the contested thermodynamic labelling of individual condensates, whereas Aili, Aqvist, Chabes and Somfai see the field as unsettled.
Whether a nitrogenase prize honours a secure structure or an unresolved mechanism (Brzezinski, Zou, Somfai).
Whether Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is a real extension of the 2010 cross-coupling prize or a repeat (Somfai versus Linke and Brzezinski).
Whether the Gray and Winkler tunnelling picture adds anything beyond Marcus theory (1992) (Aqvist's question to Brzezinski, who ranks B060 as an alternative).
attribution_disputes: B038: PROTAC concept and structure (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, with Sakamoto as coauthor of the 2001 paper) versus thalidomide-cereblon glue mechanism (Handa, Ito, Gray, Kim); eight credited names, three slots; Somfai's Crews-only variant differs from the Aili and Chabes trio.

B011: Liu alone versus Liu with Komor and Gaudelli; Nishida and Kondo's independent Target-AID cytidine-deaminase work is an unresolved priority question; Aqvist and Chabes move toward Liu alone, with Aili raising the question of whether the trainees should be named.
B003: Deamer, Bayley and Akeson versus the founding translocation claims of Branton and Kasianowicz.
B064: Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt (Brzezinski) versus Rees and Einsle (Zou); Dean and Ribbe are left out of both.
B065: Hyman and Brangwynne (Sparr) versus the full triad with Rosen, and the sequence-grammar contribution of Pappu and Mittag.
B058: Buchwald and Hartwig versus the Kosugi (and Migita) precedent, which Somfai says he cannot verify here.
maturity_disputes: B038: no PROTAC is approved. Chabes, Aili and Somfai (as a stated risk) say the confirmed mechanism matters more than approval; Brzezinski, Linke and Sparr call recognition early.
B011: replication and first clinical use are cited as maturity, but Chabes and Brzezinski note that off-target and bystander deamination is not fully characterised.
B065: Aili, Aqvist and Somfai want the debate over which condensates are true phases to settle first; Sparr says the concept-level citation does not depend on that debate.
B064: structure is mature and mechanism is not (Zou, Brzezinski, Somfai).
B003: mature in deployment (Linke, Chabes), but this is separate from the unresolved credit question.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Linke (chair): own nanowire and molecular-motor work is topically adjacent to B003, which he ranks first; he states no tie to any credited candidate and no recusal.
Brzezinski: Stockholm University colleague of Zou, who ranks B064 first; his respiratory-chain electron-transfer field is adjacent to B060 and B064.
Zou: Stockholm University colleague of Brzezinski; his electron crystallography and 3D electron diffraction work is close to the structural methods of B064; no recusal needed in his own statement.
Sparr: her lipid self-assembly and amyloid co-assembly research is scientifically close to B065 (preferred) and B018 (alternative), and she states she will disclose it again if B018 is discussed.
Aqvist: his free-energy and EVB simulation field overlaps with B036; he has not made it a preference; he also notes Warshel and ribosome and RNA connections unrelated to base editing.
Aili: thematic overlap with peptide and nanoparticle sensing, not with any shortlisted ballot directly.
No member discloses a personal or institutional tie to a credited candidate or asks for recusal.
questions_for_round2: Can anyone who ranks B038 first (Aili, Chabes) say whether the committee should write a PROTAC-only citation, add a second part for the cereblon glue strand, or defer; and, since Somfai's Crews-only variant differs, which names, if any, can be dropped without making the citation indefensible?

For B011, is Liu alone defensible against Komor, Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo, and can Aqvist, Sparr and Zou state in one sentence the chemical discovery, other than a CRISPR extension, that the citation would honour?

For B003, can the committee separate Deamer's conception from Branton and Kasianowicz's first translocation experiments well enough to support a three-name list, and is the achievement chemistry or genomics?

Should the final configuration be a single-part prize or a two-part prize, and if two-part, which pairings (B011 with B064, B011 with B065, B058 with B038) would any member besides the proposer accept?
For B064, would Brzezinski and Zou agree on a citation limited to the cofactor structure, and who among Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe must be weighed explicitly in the expert report?

How much should the lack of an approved degrader and the incomplete off-target characterisation of base editing count against B038 and B011 respectively, compared with the settled status of B003, B058 and B064?
Does any member who has not yet ranked B038, B011 or B064 first have a reason to move toward one of them, given that no position has five supporters?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows three-way support among B038, B011 and a nanopore or structure-based alternative, with no position near five votes. Positions moved during discussion (Aqvist to Liu alone, Brzezinski to nitrogenase, Zou and Sparr to two-part prizes), but each leading candidate carries an unresolved attribution or maturity question. Round 2 needs concrete citation wording and laureate sets for B038, B011, B064 and B003, and a decision on whether a two-part prize can gain a majority. I am the only supporter of B003 and have tried to represent its attribution problem as the other members described it.
